variants.name: Qt model/view: one model, several live views
variants.implementation_notes: The model owns the data and exposes it through QAbstractItemModel::data(); every view technology is a separate QAbstractItemView subclass attached with setModel(), so one QStandardItemModel or QFileSystemModel is rendered as a list, a table and a tree at the same time. Change notification replaces the Observer role of the classic structure: the model emits dataChanged/rowsInserted and the signal-slot machinery refreshes every attached view, so no view needs to know about the others. Hand-written renderer registries are unnecessary here unless the represented outputs are documents (PDF, CSV) rather than widgets.
pitfalls: QModelIndex is a temporary handle: a view that keeps one across model changes must store QPersistentModelIndex, otherwise it reads stale rows.
Views must not outlive the model (or the model must be parented to a longer-lived QObject): data() callbacks on a destroyed model are the classic Qt crash.
Answering the wrong role (DisplayRole vs EditRole, or a role the delegate never asks for) leaves cells blank while the model looks correct.

variants.name: std::variant renderer registry (framework-free)
variants.idiom_name: std::variant + std::visit over a media-type renderer table
variants.implementation_notes: Each presentation is a small type with render(const Model&, std::ostream&); a std::variant of those types is the registry (or a std::function map keyed by media type) and std::visit dispatches without a virtual hierarchy. Use this when the representations are byte streams (HTML, JSON, CSV, PDF) over a plain domain struct rather than widgets, and when the renderers should be unit-tested without a GUI toolkit; the classic virtual View base class is only worth keeping when renderers are supplied by plugins that must be swapped at run time behind a stable ABI.
pitfalls: std::visit instantiates the generic lambda for every alternative, so all renderers must share the exact call signature or the error appears as template noise, not at the call site.
A process-wide std::map/std::function registry is mutable global state: register renderers before threads start, or guard the table, otherwise a reload races with request threads.
Streaming directly to the response means headers are already sent when a renderer throws halfway; render into a buffer when a partial body cannot be tolerated.
